THE BORDER IS CLOSED.
Border security, enforcement efforts, and prosecutions have increased, resulting in zero illegal immigrants being released at the southwest border over the past six months.
Illegal entry into this country will have consequences. https://t.co/UkZyVu9Fs4
items.description: A single static talking-head clip of a CBP Border Patrol agent in uniform speaking to camera against a flat green geometric backdrop, with burned-in caption subtitles, stating zero illegal immigrants were released at the southwest border in six months. There is no music. | The United States border patrols released zero illegal immigrants into this country in the last six months. And we don't plan on breaking that pattern, we're going to continue to release zero. And look, we've done that without a single change in law. And when people know that if they're across the border illegally, they're going to be apprehended, prosecuted, and returned back to their country, they stop coming. We're sending a clear message, the border's closed, you're not going to come into this country illegally. And if you do, you're going to be apprehended, you're going to be prosecuted and returned to your home country.

I mean, you remember, this individual's application to be in this country started under the administration of Joe Biden. Matthew was killed by an illegal alien drunk driver — he died on the street at just 23.
 
While ICE officers and special agents work tirelessly to make the nation safer for Americans, ICE VOICE liaisons have a different mission.
 
VOICE victim liaisons:
 
—Help victims and their family members understand the immigration enforcement and removal process
—Provide access to social service professionals to refer victims to resources and service providers
—Help victims and their family members receive automated custody status information on criminal aliens

Toll free hotline: 855-48-VOICE, Monday-Friday 8 A.M. to 8 P.M. ET.

Celebrating the one-year anniversary of the Trump Administration's VOICE Office relaunch.

Las Vegas police arrested John Young Cotter Johnstone, an illegal alien from the UK, who police say was captured on video dragging and swinging dogs by their leashes and kicking one dog.

Johnstone faces multiple charges connected to animal abuse he allegedly committed while working at a local rescue in Nevada.

The same day Johnstone was arrested, ICE issued an immigration detainer with the Clark County Detention Center. The next day, April 2, Clark County officials honored the detainer, and ICE took custody of the alleged animal abuser.

Johnstone came to the United States under the Visa Waiver Program as a visitor. He was supposed to leave the country by Feb. 22, 2022. 

ICE secured a final order of removal. He’ll stay in ICE detention pending local charges.

items.tweet_text: Online predators don’t take time off for the holidays. Make sure your children are safe online. Hear from the team at @HSI_HQ and learn more about protecting kids from exploitation.  #12DaysofTips https://t.co/KfJ0gcogIl
items.description: Video in which HSI's Robert Lombardi speaks to camera in front of a Cyber Crimes Center (C3) backdrop, telling parents that online predators target children over the holidays and directing viewers to ice.gov/sextortion. It is a single speaker with captions and no music track. | I'm Robert Lombardi with Homeland Security Investigations, Child Exploitation and Investigations Unit. I want to remind parents that online predators are praying on our unsuspective children more than ever. Despite our guidance to kids not to talk to strangers, our kids are often doing exactly that right under our noses, in our living rooms, in the back seats of our cars, in the classrooms and more using mobile devices. Never before have our children been so vulnerable. And this is especially a concern over the holidays when our kids have more time on their hands. And criminals know it. For example, sex torsion, the act of threatening to share nude or explicit images for money is more a concern than you may think. And the current trend targets are 14 to 70-year-old children. Often the consequences are tragic. Know what your kids are doing online, talk about the risks and let them know they can come to you fo

items.tweet_text: Tis the season for shopping and staying safe online. Scammers look to your personal and financial info to make their season bright. Protect yourself and your family before shopping online with these tips from the team at @CISAgov. ⬇️ #12DaysofTips https://t.co/TAqq4gUnwz
items.description: A holiday cyber-safety video in which a CISA spokesperson wearing a Christmas sweater speaks to camera in front of a CISA step-and-repeat backdrop, advising viewers to use multi-factor authentication, shop trusted sources, and avoid phishing, ending at cisa.gov/shopsafely. It is a single speaker in a static setting, consisting of speech with no music track. | Happy Holidays! Sissa wants everyone to enjoy the holiday season, but we know that while you're breaking out your ugly sweater, bad actors are trying to steal your joy, your identity, and your money. How can you stop these scrooches in their tracks? First, always ensure you have multi-factor authentication turned on. Passwords can be hacked, so add one more level of security, your fingerprint, your face, something only you have. Second, shop through trusted sources, and watch out for fishing emails. Never give your account info out via text for email. Finally, if your password is still 12345, you're getting a hole in your stock. Learn more at sissa.gov slash shop safely. Happy Holidays! | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

According to U.S. Department of Homeland Security Blue Campaign, violent kidnapping is not the most prevalent way traffickers claim victims. Listen in to Forensic Interview Specialist Lauren G. and learn more. ⬇️ 
https://www.dhs.gov/blue-campaign/myths-and-misconceptions https://t.co/ka4h3EhyPB
items.description: An audiogram from the DHS Blue Campaign '#TacklingTrafficking' series: a static blue graphic with a play icon and audio-waveform animation plays a recorded clip of Forensic Interview Specialist Lauren G. saying that trafficking victims are typically groomed rather than kidnapped, with her words shown as text-card captions. There is no video footage and no music, only narrated interview audio over a fixed graphic. | Unlike what is portrayed in the media, trafficking victims are groomed by the trafficker and not necessarily randomly kidnapped. It is not out of the realm of possibility, however, and there have been known cases of individuals being kidnapped because they began to uncover the trafficker's scheme and decide they no longer wanted to be a part of it, so they are taken by force and held against their will. But that typically happens after the victim has been in the situation for some time. So this is another myth which has been around for many years as it was the thing to look for when kidnappings first started making way into the lives of so many families here in the United States. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tag

When I first started in the agency in 1997, I was an immigration inspector, and my office was to report to JFK. 🎁 This holiday season, shop smart and stay safe! Beware of counterfeit goods that may pose safety risks. @CBP warns that fake products—like electronics, toys, and cosmetics—can be dangerous. Always buy from trusted retailers because fake goods can lead to real dangers. ⬇️ 
https://www.cbp.gov/trade/fakegoodsrealdangers
items.description: A nearly two-minute flat 2D animated explainer about counterfeit goods for holiday shoppers, narrated throughout by an instructional voiceover (online shoppers, a shuttered 'OUT OF BUSINESS / CLOSED FOREVER' store, a burning phone, hammer-and-chains imagery) and closing on the CBP logo with a QR code. It uses cartoon styling and is narrated consumer-safety instruction. | We all buy stuff online. It's often quick, easy, and cheap. But is it always safe? In the US, we import over a billion small packages every year. And many contain fake goods that can pose real dangers. Like baby formula or cosmetics made with unknown ingredients, counterfeit prescription medications containing harmful chemicals, toys and crafts made with lead paint or other environmentally hazardous materials, faulty counterfeit car parts, bogus electronics that can catch fire. The list goes on and on. Not only can fake goods pose serious health and safety risks to you and your family, they also waste your hard-earned money, contribute to loss of American jobs, and support criminal activity like human trafficking or forced labor. US Customs and Border Protection is looking out for the American consumer. Before good

items.description: Video. A Know2Protect PSA on online child sexual exploitation built from talking-head interviews with ICE special agents (Steven Moran, Ben Miller) plus title graphics and a closing URL card. It consists of interview testimony, with no music track. | The threat of child online exploitation has never been bigger. In the 20 years I've been working, I've never seen this many leads come in. We see that taking different forms, but essentially it's when an adult offender is targeting a juvenile in the online or digital environment with the ultimate goal of some sort of sexual victimization. People don't know that this crime is happening at such an alarming rate because it is uncomfortable to talk about. Bringing it to the forefront can help prevent the crime from happening in the first place. One of the things that we always want parents to understand is predators go where the kids are. In the past playgrounds, parks, public places, that's where offenders would go. Now, the digital environment is the playground for these kids. The Notaprotect campaign will educate and empower children, teens, parents, trusted adults and policymakers to prevent and combat online child sexual exploitation

And thank you again for sharing your children's stories today.

Coast Guard transformation begins today. At today’s Commencement at the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announced a blueprint to transform the Service, Force Design 2028. Additionally, Secretary Noem announced President Trump’s nomination of Admiral Kevin Lunday as the 28th Commandant of the Coast Guard.    In her remarks to the Coast Guard Academy Class of 2025, Secretary Noem explained how this plan, under Admiral Lunday’s leadership, will revolutionize the Service’s ability to protect and serve the American people.    Learn more about the big changes coming:

 Press Release: https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4193950/secretary-noem-delivers-coast-guard-academy-commencement-address-announces-new/

Web Link: https://www.uscg.mil/leadership/commandants-initiatives/forcedesign2028/

items.description: Video. An NBC News Now sit-down interview in which Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons recounts learning about the Dallas ICE facility shooting, intercut with aerial b-roll of the scene. It is a broadcast news interview. | This hit home for you in a lot of ways, but you actually worked in the Dallas ice office, right? I did. I have so many good friends that still work there. It was really hard. I actually got the news as we were walking on set today. On a totally different related subject at CNN. You know, to hear that the ice office was on the fire, those potential fatalities. You know, it really hit home, seeing the photos today. Some of the bullets were in an office that I used to have there. It's a horrible feeling. People always ask me what's the thing that keeps me up at night. It's the safety of the men and women of ice. And this is just as bad. So take me to the beginning. What did you hear first? What are they telling you? What did you think? You know, originally we heard that there was an active shooter on site that there were potentially three people down. It wasn't as it started to unfold that we learned. It was a sniper. items.tweet_text: Anti-ICE rhetoric from elected officials puts everyone at risk. https://t.co/Xi8hpvUdmh
items.description: Video. A Newsmax remote interview with ICE Deputy Director Madison Sheehan saying that anti-ICE rhetoric from elected officials endangers agents, with b-roll of Dallas police vehicles. It is a televised news interview. | What does that sort of rhetoric mean for the agents who are working in the department? Well, let me be very clear, the job of the men and women of ISIS to enforce immigration law as it's written. Our job is not to pick winners and losers. We go out and enforce the laws that are on the books. If these lawmakers want to criticize ICE for their work, they should consider changing the law which they fully have the power to do. But President Trump and Secretary Nome empower the men and women of ICE to make sure that we are enforcing the law as it's written, securing our border and defending the homeland every single day. And I'll also say that the men and women of ICE have clear placards on their body armor. They wear their badges. They, you know, when you are interacting with an ICE officer, and that's standard to set very high with the scrutiny as well as the training that every ICE officer goes through.

It's time that this stops, that this rhetoric ends now so that the men and women of ICE can go out to the community to enforce the laws that's written. I always tell people, the laws that the men and women of ICE are enforcing are the laws that Congress has passed. items.description: A static talking-head clip of an ICE official appearing on Fox News' 'Hannity' (Hannity bug, city-skyline backdrop, 'EYE IN OHIO' chyron) discussing Operation Angel's Honor, the Laken Riley Act and over 1,000 arrests. And what I like to say to any elected official that has been going against ICE until telling people to impede us to resist ICE, the Lincoln Riley Act was enacted by the 119th Congress. It's federal law, which requires us to lock up criminal legal aliens, hold them without bond and put them in immigration proceedings. And you know, Operation Angel Honor, which was for Lincoln Riley and her family, that just shows the impact that ICE makes every day across the country.

Breaking ice to keep America moving.

Winter weather doesn’t stop commerce, or the U.S. Coast Guard. 

In 2025, @USCG facilitated the movement of $5.4T in maritime commerce and 1.8B tons of cargo across U.S. waterways. From the Northeast to the Great Lakes, our icebreaking crews ensure critical supplies reach communities, even in the harshest winter conditions. With historic funding from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the Coast Guard is recapitalizing our domestic icebreaker fleet and maximizing our return on investment across America’s waterways. 

#USCG #Icebreaking #MTS #Commerce @DHSgov @USCGNortheast @USCGGreatLakes @USCGLANTAREA

It is a televised speech with no music or added editing effects. | We can never forget that many in this room not only allowed the border invasion to happen before I got involved, but indeed they would do it all over again if they ever had the chance. If they ever got elected, they would open up those borders to some of the worst criminals anywhere in the world. The only thing standing between Americans and a wide open border right now is President Donald J. Trump and our great Republican patriots in Congress. Thank you, thank you.

items.description: A CBP officer (Monica Williams) introduces her crisis-response and wellness K9 'Izzy' in a subtitled talking-head testimonial, partly at a port of entry and partly in front of DHS and CBP flags. The tweet includes the text 'Find your purpose with us'. The video is a spoken testimonial. No music track. | My name is Monica Williams and this is Izzy. As first responders, we're exposed to so much and unfortunately we internalize a lot of that. It is very important to be able to help our workforce by promoting mental wellness. And not only do we help our employees but we also help their families and the communities that we serve. In my 27 years in this career, I am the only CVP crisis hostage negotiator and trainer for the FBI. Find out more about what Izzy and I do by reading the latest edition of the Frontline magazine.

CBP is holding the line for FIFA World Cup 2026!  CBP Officers stationed across America and around the world stand ready to process international travelers swiftly so everyone can enjoy the games.

We’ll also be making sure counterfeit merchandise is stopped, no one wants a fake jersey!

📸: @SecMullinDHS
items.description: Selfie-style talking-head video of a DHS official holding a World Cup soccer ball in an office, with caption text, speaking about CBP readiness for FIFA 2026. No music track. | Alright guys, I'm not going to sit here and pretend like I'm a big soccer fan because I am not. I'm going to sit here and brag about these different agencies. CBP, which is our custom board of protection, is going to be responsible for processing five to seven million people in a very short period of time. Now think about that. Not everyone online is who they say they are. 🚨

Kendall Carter is serving 30 years in federal prison for victimizing more than a dozen teens and children.

His case from @DHSgov’s national public awareness campaign, @Know2Protect, is a powerful reminder: Offenders often use fake profiles to manipulate and exploit kids online.

Help young people spot #FakeProfiles before harm happens using the Tips2Identify Fake Profiles resource at http://dhs.gov/know2protect/publication/fake-profiles #K2PAnniversary

🚨 @POTUS is taking executive action to protect fans from exploitative ticket scalping and bring commonsense reforms to live entertainment.

The Order directs the Federal Trade Commission to:

— Work with the Attorney General to ensure that competition laws are appropriately enforced in the concert and entertainment industry.

— Rigorously enforce the Better Online Ticket Sales (BOTS) Act and promote its enforcement by state consumer protection authorities.

— Ensure price transparency at all stages of the ticket-purchase process, including the secondary ticketing market.

— Evaluate and, if appropriate, take enforcement action to prevent unfair, deceptive, and anti-competitive conduct in the secondary ticketing market.

— The Order directs the Secretary of the Treasury and Attorney General to ensure that ticket scalpers are operating in full compliance with the Internal Revenue Code and other applicable law.

items.description: Video. They are heroes, and I hope the media has the integrity to shine a light on this story. Enough is enough with the harmful, lies and violent rhetoric. It has to stop.

Any fraud in our unemployment system WILL NOT BE TOLERATED. 

Our strike team will get to the bottom of alleged welfare fraud being committed by TPS Somalis and other groups in Minnesota. https://t.co/9Qk4898QWk
items.description: A local TV news segment ('DIGGING DEEPER / FRAUD IN MINNESOTA / TARGETED REVIEW') with an anchor reporting on a Department of Labor review of alleged unemployment-insurance fraud in Minnesota, including a full-screen quote card from Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. It is a news broadcast. | Digging deeper tonight into being termed a targeted review of potential fraud in Minnesota's unemployment insurance program. It's the latest federal probe into allegations of financial wrongdoing this one by the U.S. Department of Labor. The Secretary of Labor, writing in a letter sent to the Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development, quote, I am appalled at what we are hearing about potential fraud coming from numerous benefits programs in Minnesota. If there has been any related abuse of our U.I. systems, it will not be tolerated. End quote. U.I., by the way, is a reference to unemployment insurance. The Labor Secretary says the Department's Chicago Regional Office has started a review of its benefit payment control operations to ensure no fraud is identified in unemployment insurance programs, including those during the COVID-19 pandemic.

On January 21, ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) responded to a request from the Sherburne County Sheriff’s Office in Zimmerman, MN, to help locate a missing 7-year-old girl after an AMBER Alert. HSI teams braved sub-freezing temperatures, canvassed neighborhoods, and worked closely with local law enforcement, gathering surveillance information to aid the search.
 
On January 22, HSI was notified that the child was found safe and the alleged sexual assaulter and kidnapper, 28-year-old Joseph Andrew Bragg, was taken into custody.
 
HSI is proud to have helped bring this young girl home and ensure alleged child predators are removed from Minnesota’s streets.

items.description: Raw WBAL-TV news footage of a Maryland sheriff speaking at a podium surrounded by other uniformed sheriffs, demanding lawmakers stop blocking cooperation with ICE. And lawmakers need to wake up and realize Marylanders and the American people want public safety over politics and they're not getting it.

The SAVE America Act is overwhelmingly popular with all Americans because each provision is rooted in common sense.

The SAVE America Act has five simple requirements:

Number one, voters have to show ID to cast a ballot in an American election. 90% of Americans – including ~80% of Democrat voters – agree with this.

Number two, the SAVE America Act will require all voters to show proof of citizenship in order to register to vote.

Number three, the SAVE America Act abolishes the incredibly unsecure practice of universal mail-in ballots which throw the door wide open for fraud. Importantly, the SAVE America Act maintains exceptions for Americans to use mail-in-ballots for illness, disability, military, or travel reasons. 
Number four, the SAVE America Act permanently bans men from competing in women’s sports. 
Number five, the SAVE America Act bans transgender mutilation surgery for children.

Passing the SAVE America Act is the most important thing that Republicans can do right now to strengthen election integrity.

Through Operation Pacific Viper, they interdicted over 22,000 lbs of cocaine worth an estimated $250M, a record for our HITRON teams that keeps drugs off our streets. Spearheading the nation’s efforts to interdict dark fleet oil tankers, CGC Munro’s shadowed the Motor Tanker Bella 1 across the Atlantic, culminating in the vessel’s seizure.

Unmatched impact in defense of America by a dedicated crew. Read more: https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4426962/coast-guard-cutter-munro-crew-returns-home-after-119-day-multi-mission-patrol-m/

items.tweet_text:
Our ICE officers and agents are HEROES.

On March 25, 2026, an ICE agent helping to support @TSA operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York jumped into action to help save the life of a one-year-old child experiencing a medical emergency.

The heroic actions of this officer began when a one-year-old child became unresponsive in the arms of his father, unable to breathe for almost two minutes. CCTV review shows a passenger in a TSA Precheck line holding his one-year-old in his arms when the child’s arms go lifeless; panic ensues, and the father is seen scrambling around the area, and calling for help.  

The agent working at his post, heard the screams from the father and other passengers and sprinted to the scene. The father handed the child to the officer, who then assessed the unresponsive child and began performing the Heimlich maneuver. After a few seconds, the child started breathing again. EMS personnel arrived on scene with medical equipment to further monitor and re-assess the child. The child was re-assessed and determined to be healthy enough to fly.

Nine U.S. citizens and illegal aliens, including two John Does, were charged in a federal crackdown on benefit fraud schemes in Massachusetts by ICE @HSINewEngland and its partners.

The accused allegedly used stolen identities belonging to U.S. citizens from Puerto Rico to steal more than $1.1 million in taxpayer-funded programs — including SNAP, MassHealth and Social Security benefits.

Stolen IDs were first used to obtain government-issued identification, including Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles credentials and, in some instances, U.S. passports, which were then used to apply for and receive public benefits.

An Ohio man who led police on an hours-long chase in 2024 was sentenced to 30 years in prison March 24 for child sexual abuse crimes following an ICE HSI Detroit probe.

Johnathan Brown, 34, secretly recorded young girls, hiding outside bedroom windows and placing cameras inside a laundry basket to record minors after they exited showers. 

Brown also groomed a teenager, beginning when she was 15, eventually filming himself having sex with the victim. 

Special thanks to the Butler Township Police Department, Miami Valley Human Trafficking Task Force and @OSHP.
items.description: Horizontal video. He had outside bedroom windows and put cameras and laundry baskets to record minors getting out of the shower. He then told the victims that he needed the videos for quote medical reasons. Court records say that he also groomed a 15-year-old and sold sexually explicit pictures threatening self-harm to get that teen to cooperate. In August of 2024, he led police on a wild chase around Dayton before driving onto a moving train and starting the SWAT situation. Police couldn't get Brown out until they used tear gas and a canine to bring him down. Brown pleaded guilty to the pornography charges back in October.

—Aggravated sexual assault of a child, 1st degree felony: 75 years and a $10,000 fine
—Promoting prostitution of a child under 18, 1st degree felony: 20 years
—Compelling prostitution of a child under 18, 1st degree felony: 20 years
—Sexual performance of a child under 14, 1st degree felony: 99 years
—Possession of CSAM/video, 2nd degree felony: 20 years
—Possession of child CSAM/video, 1st degree felony: 75 years and a $5,000 fine

items.tweet_text:
Every American needs to see this.

18-year-old Sheridan Gorman was brutally murdered in Chicago — just blocks from her college dorm — by an illegal alien who should never have been here.

At 1:30 a.m., while watching the northern lights near Lake Michigan, a masked gunman opened fire. Sheridan warned her friends and ran — only making it about 40 feet before she was shot in the back and killed in cold blood.

Her devastated parents are calling it what it is: "It was a preventable murder."

The killer was released into the U.S. under Biden, arrested for shoplifting in sanctuary Chicago, released without notifying ICE, and then skipped court.

Her father demands accountability: "When someone commits a crime and they've been here illegally, there needs to be cooperation... He should've been handed over to the feds."

Open borders and sanctuary policies killed Sheridan Gorman.

This is the human cost of failed leadership.

items.tweet_text: .@SecRubio: "The Chinese side said they are not in favor of militarizing the Straits of Hormuz and they're not in favor of a tolling system, and that's our position... It's good that we have alliance, or at least agreement, on that point." https://t.co/ehhk7pbBgv
items.description: NBC News Now sit-down interview of Secretary Rubio (US flag behind, NBC logo) discussing the Straits of Hormuz and a UN resolution on Iran. Static interview shot with reporter, continuous talking, no music. | Did President Trump raise the issue of Iran with China? He did, and it was important because the Chinese side said they are not in favor of militarizing the Straits of Hormuz, and they're not in favor of a tolling system. And that's our position. We will never support an Iranian tolling system in the Straits of Hormuz, nor do we think they have a right to put minds in international waters. And so it's good that we have alliance, or at least agreement on that point. I think the fundamental question is what are we going to do about it? We have a resolution now before the United Nations, in which 100 and something countries have co-signed. The Bahrainis are the sponsor, but we're strongly behind it, and we've been pushing very hard on it. And it very clearly makes those points. So we hope the Chinese will vote for it. So right now we haven't gotten their commitment to vote for it yet at the United Nations. Maybe that'll change after today's meeting. I don't know. | Reviewed video

.@AFergusonFTC explains how the @WHFraudTF is using AI-driven technological solutions to stop fraudulent payments from leaving federal agencies:

"So much of this money that goes out the door leaves the country... it's got to stay in the agency, and AI is supercharging this." https://t.co/KQJKfTxZUk
items.description: FTC's Ferguson in a seated interview describing AI fraud-detection systems used by the White House Fraud Task Force. Sustained spoken transcript, no music. | So, all of the agencies are supposed to have anti-fraud prevention systems in place. The bi administration turned a lot of those off and let them languish. And what we were able to do basically, sort of like building on the doge effort, is work with these agencies with the data that they have, the data that other agencies have, and publicly available data, and build technological solutions, most of which are AI-driven that can take all of these data. And so when a claims payment request comes in, basically AI puts up a flag and says, very likely fraudulent. And all of the agencies have administrative authority to withhold those payments until they know that this is a real person that's actually qualifying for this request. If you have to do that by hand, if you have to have individuals go out and figure all these out, the money just goes out the door, and then you have to get the doge to chase it and they can't get it all back. So using these advanced automated technological solutions, that's the way you supercharge the effort

items.tweet_text:
.@POTUS: "From 1776 to 2026, America has always stood as a great and moral cause. Our warriors are no mere mercenaries, they are guardian angels who stride across the battlefields of history and stand watch over the highest and most beautiful planes the human spirit has ever seen—holding the line between liberty and tyranny, between civilization and barbarism, between good and evil. Wherever the American Soldier walks, wherever he fights... and wherever he falls, he does it for the destiny of a nation like no other... and for the fate of Freedom on this earth...

By their deaths, those who have gone before us in battle have redeemed the promise of our Founding for each future generation.

They've not just made the Ultimate Sacrifice, they have offered the Ultimate Proof that we Americans do indeed love Liberty. We do cherish the self-government given to us by our forefathers. We do believe with all our souls in the mission that God has given to America. And we do intend with all our strength and heart to hold high the torch our heroes handed to us—and we will never, ever let it fall."

items.tweet_text:
.@POTUS: "Scripture tells us, 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful servants.' 400,000 souls rest on these grounds... in this sacred soil, which was first consecrated in the hour of America’s greatest Division to be an eternal symbol of our National Unity. It cannot be by chance alone that the very first servicemember laid to rest here, in this place of supreme sacrifice, was a Union Soldier by the name of Private Christman—Private William Henry Christman of Pennsylvania, who died at 19 years old...

🚨AMO Black Hawk disabling fire ends vessel pursuit🚨

On May 13, AMO aircrews detected a suspicious 25-foot Yola-type vessel northwest of Puerto Rico, carrying three individuals and visible packages. Our teams maintained continuous aerial surveillance, tracking the vessel through the night.

The next evening, the San Juan Marine Unit launched a coordinated interdiction operation. Two Coastal Interceptor Vessels and multiple aircraft moved in, guided by constant vectors from our aircrews.

At 9:51 p.m., the targeted vessel was intercepted north of San Juan. The suspects tried to evade capture and began dumping contraband into the water. In a decisive moment, the AMO Black Hawk crew deployed Air Disabling Fire, stopping the vessel cold.

Three Dominican Republic nationals were taken into custody, and five bales containing 391 lbs. of cocaine were seized and transferred to the Homeland Security Task Force. This operation highlights our relentless commitment to securing America’s borders and keeping dangerous drugs off our streets. 

Check out the full video here: https://ow.ly/TVYb50Z5kFS#SecuringAmerica 

#AMO #BorderSecurity #Teamwork

Janet Napolitano, Obama’s DHS Secretary, openly described their policy: catch people near the border within about 100-120 miles, prioritize criminals and security threats, and let everyone else settle in deeper into the country. That wasn’t an accident, it was the deliberate system.

They even cooked the books to earn Obama the “Deporter in Chief” title, reclassifying a ton of quick border turnarounds as formal removals to inflate the stats, while interior enforcement actually dropped sharply over his terms.

Look at who’s running DHS today: they came up through that exact system. No wonder @RealTomHoman and @CBPCommissioner are falling back on what they know. That’s why we’re not getting the mass deportations voters demanded.

Whoever sidelined @StephenM blocked what the American people voted for. 

The old incentives are still baked in, and the swamp protects itself through quiet institutional memory…

📱Random
📱Unique

items.tweet_text: We know of no threat to the public. If we learn of any cause for concern, we will take action and communicate immediately with the American public. https://t.co/oddf59jFSH
items.description: Video. A TV 'Exit Interview' clip of Secretary Mayorkas (talking head with a subtitle bar) discussing drone sightings over New Jersey and asking Congress to expand DHS authorities. It is a broadcast interview, with no music. | And let me restate what we've said previously. It's very important. We know of no threat to people's security. And if we learn of any cause for concern, we will take action and we will communicate immediately with the American public. There are, and there have been thousands and thousands of drones flown across the United States for years. All drones, recreational drones, law enforcement drones. I spoke with an expert yesterday who has recorded over his home in California over the past six years, more than 13,000 drone detections. And so this is actually not a new phenomenon. What we need in the federal government is we need our authorities to catch up with the development of drone activity over the last 10 years. And so we have asked Congress for not only an extension of our authorities, but an expansion of them. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.description: Horizontal video, a repost of a 'How It Started vs. How It's Going' clip. It shows a split-screen of Fox News footage comparing VP Harris's 2021 Guatemala 'do not come' speech (labeled 'How it started... All Talk') with Sec. Noem standing in front of caged detainees at El Salvador's CECOT prison, then two plain blue static text cards reading 'TODAY, WE'RE PUTTING CRIMINALS BEHIND BARS' and 'UNDER PRESIDENT TRUMP AND SECRETARY NOEM, DHS PUTS AMERICA FIRST'. The audio is the anchors and officials speaking, with no music. | I want to be clear to folks in this region who are thinking about making that dangerous trek to the United States, Mexico border. Do not come. Do not come. First of all, do not come to our country illegally. You will be removed and you will be prosecuted. But know that this facility is one of the tools in our toolkit that we will use if you commit crimes against the American people. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

It is a speech excerpt with no music, stylization, or editing. | But such horrendous imbalances have devastated our industrial base and put our national security at risk. I don't blame these other countries at all for this calamity. I blame former presidents and past leaders who weren't doing their job. They let it happen and they let it happen to an extent that nobody can even believe. That's why effective at midnight, we will impose a 25 percent tariff on all foreign-made automobiles. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text:
What do you get when you cross a previously convicted carjacker with a ghost gun? A FOOT PURSUIT, OF COURSE.

When you’ve just been released from a 3-year prison sentence for carjacking, you probably (definitely) shouldn’t be packing a firearm.

A #PremierSector agent saw a single CHP officer on a stop with two subjects and decided to stop and assist because teamwork makes the dream work. As our agent attempted to conduct a Terry frisk for officer safety, one subject decided he was going to test his 100-yard dash time and sprinted into an alfalfa field to get away. 

He must have thought the weapon and ammo he was carrying was invisible while he was tossing it into the field in front of our pursuing agent. Guess what? We saw it!! 👀

After taking the subject into custody, our agent turned him and his recovered ghost gun 👻🔫 back over to CHP. This felon must really miss prison cafeteria food because he’s working extra hard to go back. 

Video courtesy of David Abatti and @pinshi_metishi_760

#CBP #DHS #BorderPatrol #CHP #FelonFails

items.tweet_text: SPLASHDOWN IN TEXAS! On 5/27, smugglers tried to outsmart the U.S. Border Patrol with a bold move—floating a pickup truck loaded with suspicious bundles across the Rio Grande on a homemade raft. Once on U.S. soil, they made a break for it. But as agents closed in, the driver veered back and plunged the truck into the river in a desperate attempt to escape. Chaos followed as individuals scrambled in the water to retrieve the suspected narcotics—but USBP agents acted fast. They recovered 6 bundles of marijuana weighing nearly 250 lbs. Smugglers are getting bolder, but USBP always stands at the ready.

Maritime Safety and Security Team (MSST) Honolulu 91107 stands at the forefront of the Coast Guard’s mission to protect America’s interests.

Specializing in Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security, MSST Honolulu conducts high-risk vessel escorts, enforces safety and security zones, and executes maritime pursuit operations to prevent illegal activity. Applying our unique authorities and capabilities, they are at the leading edge of our operations to control, secure, and defend U.S. borders and maritime approaches.

MSST Honolulu’s presence underscores the Coast Guard’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific, strengthens regional stability, and plays a key role in advancing U.S. interests in a dynamic and strategic region.

@Sec_Noem  unveiled Force Design 2028: a bold, once-in-a-generation plan to transform the 234-year-old Coast Guard into a modern, mission-ready force. 🇺🇸

Thank you, Secretary Noem, for your leadership and bold vision to transform the Coast Guard through Force Design 2028.

Through FD 2028, the Service is revolutionizing how it functions and operates to ensure decisive advantage over adversaries. Focused on four campaigns - People, Organization, Contracting and Acquisition, and Technology - FD 2028 is re-shaping the Coast Guard into a stronger, more ready and capable fighting force.

Coast Guard crews around the country work diligently to prevent illegal narcotics from entering the United States.

Coast Guard Cutter Kimball exemplified these operations during a recent patrol from February through April, during which they conducted multiple drug interdictions off the coasts of Mexico and Central and South America. This culminated in Kimball offloading more than $191 million worth of cocaine in April.

As the Coast Guard continues to surge assets across our southern border and maritime approaches, our crews have been leading the fight against drug cartels and Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCO). The dedicated efforts of Kimball – and men and women across the Coast Guard – are directly impacting the ability of cartels and TCOs to smuggle illicit drugs into our communities. 

📷PA3 Avery Tibbets & MST3 Austin Wiley

@DHSgov @USCGPACAREA @USCGHawaiiPac 

#USCG #USCGHawaii #IndoPacific #druginterdiction

items.tweet_text:
This is what generational change looks like. Yesterday, U.S. Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) Storis transited the Panama Canal, marking a significant milestone on its maiden voyage towards its future homeport in Juneau.
 
After departing the Panama Canal, Storis met three recently decommissioned 110’ Island-Class Patrol Boats from Alaska – USCGCs Liberty, Mustang, and Naushon. These are the last of the storied 110’s, being succeeded by the modern Sentinel-class Fast Response Cutters.
 
Today’s passage exemplifies the Coast Guard’s transformation under Force Design 2028. As the United States’ third polar icebreaker, Storis will bring innovative capabilities and crewing to assure access to the polar regions and protect U.S. sovereignty. As the Service modernizes its fleet and infrastructure, Storis will continue the return on America’s investment in the Coast Guard. @USCGPACAREA @USCGAlaska @DHSgov 

#USCG #Storis #PolarOperations #PanamaCanal #ForceDesign2028 #ArcticPresence #IcebreakerFleet

Value to Nation: Across the Coast Guard’s range of missions, our men and women are dedicated to keeping Americans safe and delivering on the Nation’s historic investment in the Service. We continue to surge resources to control, secure, and defend 31,000 miles of U.S. maritime borders — where defense of America begins.

We are combating foreign terrorist organizations, cartels, and transnational organized crime.

We facilitate commerce vital to economic security and strategic mobility.

We are always ready to respond to a crisis or contingency that may come with little or no warning.

Continuing our transformation through Force Design 2028, the Coast Guard remains focused on maximizing value to the Nation through the most agile, capable, and responsive maritime fighting force.

A major milestone this week in the Coast Guard’s drug interdiction efforts: Since January 20, we’ve seized over 242,000 pounds of cocaine. With as little as 1.2g being enough to kill someone, that’s 91 million potentially lethal doses.  

@USCG continues to surge forces along the southern border and maritime approaches. The strategy is working. Applying our unique authorities and capabilities, we’ve stopped over 100% percent more cocaine than we did in 2024.

Bravo Zulu to the men and women of the Coast Guard. Through their tireless efforts – and close coordination with interagency partners – we are seizing record amounts of illegal drugs and making America safer. 
 
Read more: https://www.dhs.gov/news/2025/07/15/coast-guard-seizes-over-240000-pounds-cocaine-doubling-amount-interdicted-over

#USCG #druginterdiction #ValueToNation @DHSgov

Yesterday, @USCG commissioned the Fast Response Cutter Earl Cunningham, honoring Boatswain’s Mate Second Class Earl Cunningham, who gave his life in 1936 during a heroic rescue on Lake Michigan.

Cunningham’s courage and legacy now inspire the mission of this cutter, which will strengthen our capabilities to defend Alaska’s maritime border and respond to crises. Through historic investment in the Coast Guard, we have ordered additional Fast Response Cutters.

Welcome aboard, USCGC Earl Cunningham!  

Follow @USCGArctic for more news about the Cunningham and its crew.

Read more and hear from the CO here: https://www.mycg.uscg.mil/News/Article/4271141/if-not-us-who-a-conversation-with-the-co-of-our-newest-fast-response-cutter/

Mission Ready: V-BAT Completes Operational Testing with the U.S. Coast Guard!

Aboard USCGC Stone, crews are operating VBAT (a vertical takeoff drone) and Remote Aerial Systems that provide real-time surveillance and targeting support. These tools expand reach and sharpen awareness to identify narco-terrorist networks and stop drug smuggling at sea.

Through Force Design 2028, we are accelerating tech to the frontlines—giving our crews the decisive edge.

#USCG #TipoftheSpear #Technology #AlwaysReady #ForceDesign2028 @DHSgov 

Watch the full video on our YouTube: https://youtu.be/8vY8dkbxN2M?si=lYrXhHBvNV4TCpqB

Aboard Coast Guard Cutter Stone, Health Services Technicians ensure the crew remains medically ready to operate during sustained missions at sea. CGC Stone set drug interdiction records through Operation Pacific Viper, offloading over 49,000 pounds of cocaine following a patrol in the Eastern Pacific. Petty Officer Harrison ensured the crew was ready to perform, respond, and remain on mission.
 
Being Always Ready depends on every crew member. Become part of the Semper Paratus legacy. Join the Coast Guard ➡️ http://GoCoastGuard.com

Behind every successful patrol is a crew that keeps the cutter operational.

Aboard @USCG Cutter Stone, Machinery Technicians keep propulsion, power, and critical systems operating to ensure the cutter remains ready to operate and respond. Through Operation Pacific Viper, CGC Stone and other @USCG units have interdicted over 170K pounds of cocaine since early August. That took a total team effort. As a Machinery Technician, Smallboat Engineer, and Boarding Team Member, Petty Officer Fair ensured CGC Stone was always ready to operate and deliver results wherever the mission took the crew.

What can you bring to being Semper Paratus? Find out at http://GoCoastGuard.com

#USCG #MemberHighlight #SemperParatus @DHSgov @USCGPACAREA @USCGLANTAREA

A ready @USCG starts with a healthy workforce.

Through Force Design 2028, we’re forging a more agile, capable, and responsive maritime fighting force. To accelerate that effort, the Service is launching the Physical Readiness Program, to include mandated daily physical training and body composition compliance.

Nutrition is a key element. Senior Chief Sonata Haley shares practical nutrition tips that support energy, focus, and resilience, because readiness begins with taking care of our people.

Proper nutrition means you won’t just be fit for duty, you’ll be fit for life.

#USCG #ForceDesign2028 #Readiness

America’s only heavy icebreaker continues to deliver where no other ship can operate.

As we modernize our domestic icebreaker fleet, we continue to facilitate commerce in response to ice impacts to navigation on our waterways.

How did #USCG Cutter Polar Star celebrate its 50th birthday? By breaking a cruise ship free from Antarctic ice.

This was just one moment in the successful 55-day Operation Deep Freeze. The Polar Star’s crew also carved a 7-mile channel, enabling the delivery of millions of gallons of fuel and a new pier for the U.S. Antarctic Program. As the United States' only heavy polar icebreaker, the Polar Star's performance underscores its indispensable role in maintaining strategic year-round access to the polar regions. This is global impact – facilitating commerce and defending America’s national interests in these critical and challenging environments.

After 14,000 miles, the crew is heading home. Bravo Zulu on a historic deployment!

Read more: https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4431373/us-coast-guard-cutter-polar-star-completes-operation-deep-freeze-2026-mission-d/

items.tweet_text:
DETAINER ISSUED FOR ALLEGED NC MURDERER

Venezuelan national Angelvis Jesus Quintero Fernandez was arrested for allegedly shooting a man to death in Mecklenburg County, NC, Jan. 24.

ICE issued a detainer on him with the Mecklenburg County Jail March 23 to prevent him from reentering the community.
items.description: Horizontal video. A local TV news package about a Venezuelan national charged in a Mecklenburg County, NC murder. It includes a stand-up reporter, the suspect's mugshot, and on-screen fact bullets. It is a broadcast news clip reposted by ICE, with no music track. | We just learned Fernandez is being held without bond and has a court-appointed public defender. Fernandez is facing first-degree murder charges and it is related to the deadly shooting of 44-year-old Ludvin Guzman Morales along Central Avenue on January 24. Court records show that Fernandez was arrested yesterday and investigators say a break in the case came just days ago when officers responded to an attempted murder on Albumor Road. During the investigation, police say they found a gun inside Fernandez's car. They say he later admitted to shooting the victim after examining that weapon detectives believe it may be linked to the shooting of Guzman Morales. Now Fernandez also has an ice detainer meaning he could be taken into federal custody here at the Mecklenburg County Court House Fernandez is expected to be seen again on April 14th.

Two years after the tragic collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, we pause to honor the lives lost and remember the resilience of the Baltimore community. 

From the first moments, @USCG coordinated a complex response alongside our federal, state, and local counterparts. Bringing a range of authorities and capabilities to bear, we established a unified command, deployed advanced underwater sonar drones to search for victims in hazardous conditions, and guided the monumental effort to safely clear the 700-foot Fort McHenry Federal Channel.  

The Key Bridge collapse underscored the significance of America’s Marine Transportation System, our vital network of ports and waterways. As efforts continue toward rebuilding the Key Bridge, the Coast Guard is steadfast in our resolve to respond to contingencies and facilitate commerce vital to economic prosperity.

On April 2, @USCG Cutter Waesche, MH-60 Jayhawk, and HC-130 Hercules aircrews rescued five people from fishing vessel Ocean Bay after it grounded and took on water near Umnak Island.  

A Good Samaritan vessel arrived first on scene and relayed vital communications before our crews arrived and safely hoisted all five mariners from the vessel. 

This is integrated search and rescue in action. On the worst of days, in the harshest environments, we're Always Ready. 

Read more: https://bit.ly/48okN9q

LATEST CONSPIRATOR SENTENCED IN 13-YEAR ICE HSI ILLICIT SOFTWARE PROBE

A Florida woman got 22 months in prison and a $50,000 fine March 2 for trafficking illicit certificate of authenticity labels that bear Microsoft software activation codes.

Heidi Richards was sentenced in a 13-year, nationwide ICE @HSIKansasCity-led probe into a trafficking network that collectively harvested and resold at a discount over 600,000 illicit key codes worth over $900 million.

The labels and codes made counterfeit software appear legitimate.

The investigation so far includes $20.6 million in seized assets, as well as arrests, indictments and convictions of nine major distributors. DOJ calls this the largest software prosecution in its history.

Established on May 28, 1924, the USBP was born from a critical need to secure our expanding borders.

From its early days, with agents often providing their own horses and navigating vast, rugged terrains, the Border Patrol's mission has continuously evolved. Through eras of Prohibition, shifting immigration policies, and the complexities of national security, agents have adapted, utilizing new technologies and strategies to meet the challenges of their time. This rich history is a testament to a century of unwavering dedication and resilience.

Today, that legacy lives on through the brave men and women who stand guard 24/7. Their commitment ensures the integrity of our borders and the safety of our communities. As we reflect on 102 years of service, we honor every agent who has contributed to this vital mission. Happy 102nd Birthday, U.S. Border Patrol!

#USBP #BorderPatrol #NationalSecurity #HistoryOfService #Anniversary

items.tweet_text:
🚨ICYMI - 240 LIVES SAVED DURING ILLEGAL MARITIME MIGRATION ATTEMPT! 

On May 31, a Jacksonville Air and Marine Branch Multi-Role Enforcement Aircraft detected a surface target of interest about 65 nautical miles south of the Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI).

Air Interdiction Agents relayed information to TCI authorities and OPBAT partners, providing updated position, course, and speed reports.

The AMO aircrew conducted a successful over-the-air handoff of the STOI to a U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) aircraft.

USCG aircrew reported the vessel had lost one engine, was slowly taking on water, and occupants were observed bailing 3–5 gallons of water per minute.

At approximately 9:00 pm, USCG reported the vessel was dead in the water and occupants continued to bail water using buckets.

TCI authorities declared a search and rescue case due to increased risk of capsizing and launched four maritime surface assets. 

At approximately 1:00 a.m. on June 1, TCI authorities successfully rescued/interdicted the STOI.

TCI authorities reported a total of 240 migrants onboard: 191 adult males, 44 adult females, and 5 minors.

The passengers and crew were taken by Turks and Caicos authorities and did not reach U.S. soil.

WATCH: Nighttime Interdiction Takes Down 3 Dominican Republic Nationals!

On June 9, at approximately 11:00 PM local time, a Caribbean Air and Marine Branch Multi-Role Enforcement Aircraft detected a Target of Interest—a 19-foot Yola-type vessel with one outboard engine, three people onboard, and no navigation lights—about 29 nautical miles north of Arecibo, Puerto Rico. The suspicious vessel was tracked and monitored through coordinated air and marine surveillance, with a NASOC DHC-8 aircrew also providing coverage surveillance.
 
The San Juan Marine Unit launched a Coastal Interceptor Vessel to intercept, guided by real-time updates from the Caribbean Air and Marine Operations Center. After persistent tracking, Marine Interdiction Agents intercepted the vessel north of Camuy, Puerto Rico. Three Dominican Republic nationals and electronic devices were seized and transferred to the Homeland Security Task Force for further processing. This operation underscores the vigilance and teamwork of our air and marine units in protecting our maritime borders! #BorderSecurity

🚨40 Illegal Aliens Interdicted Near Western Puerto Rico!
 
On June 6, at 12:28 a.m., the Caribbean Air and Marine Operations Center detected a target of interest west of Desecheo Island. CAMOC relayed the information to a National Air Security Operations Center DHC-8 aircrew, who located the 25 to 30 foot rustic vessel with multiple people onboard.
 
The vessel appeared disabled and unable to make way. The DHC-8 aircrew maintained surveillance and guided a U.S. Coast Guard cutter to the location. As the cutter approached, the vessel began moving toward Puerto Rico’s shoreline.
 
The USCG intercepted the vessel at around 2 a.m. Forty individuals were apprehended - 36 nationals from the Dominican Republic (34 adult males, 2 adult females), three Haitian nationals (all adult males), and one Uzbekistan national (adult male).
 
Incredible teamwork to stop this maritime attempt! AMO continues to work alongside federal, state, and international partners to disrupt smuggling operations and safeguard national security!

Result: 3,960 pounds of marijuana seized and 2 Ecuadorian suspects detained.
